purpose: Defensive local materialization queue for public AI-runtime repair references.

selection_policy.coverage: one adjacent AI runtime and one framework/runtime source
selection_policy.priority: small safe fixtures, explicit arithmetic/shape contracts, official source URL
selection_policy.strict_rule: No case becomes strict-eligible from this plan alone.

cases.why_selected: Closest external reference to existing CWE-190 and zero-extent arithmetic fixtures.
materialization_steps: Record official PR base/head commit IDs from the PR metadata.
Materialize only the changed source files and a clean local worktree.
Run cwe_detect on the before/after arithmetic scope.
Create bounded small-shape fixtures; do not use huge allocations or OOM inputs.
Run contract analysis, repair_plan, symmetry/matrix where paired paths exist.
Build the smallest available local test target and run defensive two-sided verification.
Record source, patch, binary, and runtime hashes in the case evidence object.

cases.why_selected: Adds a MindSpore/Gitee case and tests whether dynamic-shape overflow can be verified without unsafe resource pressure.
materialization_steps: Record official Gitee PR base/head revision identifiers.
Materialize the changed Python/C++ files and exact dependency revision.
Map the dynamic-shape arithmetic to a bounded CWE-190 contract.
Use tiny dimensions and explicit overflow checks; never trigger multi-gigabyte allocation.
Run detector, contract analysis, and repair_plan on the changed scope.
Run available unit-level validation; runtime remains REVIEW if a full local build is unavailable.
Store Gitee URL, revisions, fixture hashes, and missing evidence in provenance.

safety_constraints: no exploit chain or real executor
no OOM, huge allocation, or resource-exhaustion sample
a local crash is evidence of a preimage defect, never a successful rejection
